key_insight: A proposed fault-tolerant quantum processor replaces per-qubit external control with a constant number of instruction wires and a fixed, clocked local circuit.
engineering_relevance: The architecture could reduce external wiring demands for scalable quantum hardware, while trading control flexibility for on-chip information routing and execution overhead.
method: Route quantum information through a planar array using local gates.
Repeat a fabrication-fixed, geometrically local depth-3 circuit, with instructions entering through a few externally connected qubits.
Prove fault tolerance below a universal physical-noise threshold, assuming a noiseless global clock.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical threshold theorem—not hardware measurements—with n physical qubits supporting n/polylog(n/ε) logical qubits and time n/polylog(n/ε) per logical gate.
watch_item: The noiseless global clock is an idealization; the faster polylog(n/ε)-time variant additionally assumes instantaneous, noiseless on-chip classical broadcasts.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
